findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor on a datetime and crashes
findings.body: The audit log endpoint uses `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a `datetime`. `get_item_key` then calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on it, which raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls this key for every non-empty result set, so any `optimized_pagination=true` request that returns rows fails with a 500. The paginator needs datetime handling like `DateTimePaginator` (or should subclass it).

findings.title: value_from_cursor returns a raw number for a datetime column
findings.body: `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` (an int of milliseconds) unchanged. `build_queryset` then adds `WHERE datetime <= %s` with that integer. Comparing a timestamp column to an integer either raises a database error or filters wrongly. Paging past the first page with the optimized paginator is therefore broken.

findings.title: Negative queryset slicing is unsupported in Django and raises errors
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start. Django QuerySets reject negative indexing with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`. Any user can send a cursor like `0:-5:0` with `optimized_pagination=true` and trigger an unhandled 500. The comment saying "Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, as the other paginators do.

findings.title: BasePaginator still passes negative offsets through for prev cursors
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps only forward cursors. A client-supplied prev cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `123:-10:1`) still reaches `queryset[negative:...]` and raises an unhandled exception, giving a 500 on every endpoint that uses `Paginator`/`DateTimePaginator`. Separately, silently clamping forward cursors hides malformed input. Negative offsets should raise `BadPaginationError` for both directions.

findings.title: Uses request.user.is_superuser instead of an active-superuser check
findings.body: The gate checks `request.user.is_superuser`, which is true even when the superuser session is not active (no sudo/active-superuser cookie). Sentry normally uses `is_active_superuser(request)` for these checks. As written, a superuser account without an elevated session gets the privileged paginator path, bypassing the standard superuser activation controls.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None
findings.body: For a non-superuser request, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` can be `None`, for example for staff or API-token access paths that pass `OrganizationAuditPermission` without membership. In that case this line raises `AttributeError`, so the endpoint returns a 500 even when `optimized_pagination` is not requested.

findings.title: Misleading security/safety comments about negative offsets
findings.body: The comments claim negative offsets "enable access to data beyond normal pagination bounds" and are "safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level". They also claim the ORM handles negative slicing. None of this is accurate. The `cursors.py` comment likewise says negative offsets are now allowed, but no behavior changed there. These comments mislead future maintainers about both safety and behavior.

findings.title: No tests for new paginator or endpoint branch
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, the `optimized_pagination` branch in the audit log endpoint, and the changed offset handling in `BasePaginator` have no tests. A basic test would have caught that the optimized path crashes on datetime keys and on negative offsets.
